title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the 1981 continuation of La Longue Marche, which studies the Galois action on the profinite fundamental group of U_{0,3} = P^1 − {0,1,∞} over Q.

Objects in play:
- Γ_Q = Gal(Q̄/Q).
- Π_Q^ét: the arithmetic fundamental group, an extension of Γ_Q by π̂_1 of the geometric fibre.
- 𝓜 = N_{1,1}^ét and 𝓜^!: groups attached to the modular / U_{0,3} situation.
- G_{ρ,σ} ≃ Ẑ^*·M̂: semidirect products of the units Ẑ^* with a large module, essentially a completed group ring such as Ẑ[[Ẑ^2]]-type objects. Its image of interest is N_σ^♮ ≃ Ẑ^*·Ẑ = Aff(Ẑ), the normalizer of a cyclic (inertia-like) subgroup.

Previous page: Grothendieck had split the basic homomorphism 𝓜 → 𝓜_{ρ,σ} into two pieces:
- (325) 𝓜 → G_{ρ,σ}, restricting to 𝓜^! → G_{ρ,σ}^{⇆} ≃ Ẑ^*·M̂;
- (326) Π_Q^ét → N_σ ≃ Ẑ^*·Ẑ.
Piece (325) had been characterized arithmetico-geometrically in §13, through the reduced map (327) 𝓜_{0,3} → G̃_{ρ,σ}. Concretely this is the Galois/monodromy action on the tower of Fermat curves x^N + y^N = 1. These are the abelian (Z/N)^2-covers of U_{0,3}, so the tower corresponds to the maximal abelian quotient of the commutator subgroup, i.e. the metabelian quotient of π̂_1. The limit of their Tate modules, T_∞(Ferm), is a module over Ẑ[[Ẑ^2]]. This is the object Ihara later studied ('universal power series for Jacobi sums').

This page:
1. A methodological remark. The 'current viewpoint' aims to make algebraic geometry essentially of finite type over Q explicit in terms of actions of profinite groups. Conversely, the homomorphism (327), built 'à la force du poignet' (by brute force), can be read as a group-theoretic description of the Fermat tower. This is the anabelian programme stated in both directions.
2. A remaining task: give an arithmetico-geometric interpretation of the homomorphism Γ_Q (⊂ Π_Q^ét) → Ẑ^*·Ẑ induced by (325).
3. The answer. Use the embedding N_σ^♮ ↪ G_{ρ,σ}^♮ ≃ Ẑ^*·M̂. The map (326) restricted to Γ_Q then equals the composite
   Γ_Q --κ_{1/2}--> 𝓜^! --(Fermat)--> G_{ρ,σ}^♮.
   Here κ_{1/2} is the section of π_1(U_{0,3,Q}) → Γ_Q given by the rational point z = 1/2. That point is the fixed point of z ↦ 1−z, a special point of the S_3-symmetry.
4. The page ends announcing the commutative diagram (328), which is on the next page.

Mathematically (next page): the Galois action on the fibre of the Fermat tower over 1/2 is a torsor under T_∞(Ferm) ⊗ M̂. Its class realizes (326). Concretely, points of F_N above 1/2 involve N-th roots of 1/2 (or of −1/2, −1 in the coordinates of U_1). So the map Γ_Q → Aff(Ẑ) should be (cyclotomic character χ, Kummer cocycle of 2 up to sign/normalization).

In modern terms: specialize the metabelian (Fermat / Ihara) Galois representation along the rational section at 1/2 to recover a Kummer-type character.
errors: No mathematical error is visible on this page.

The ingredients are only identified, not computed. The precise Kummer character (of 2, −2, or −1/2) and the normalization of the torsor are not determined on this page.

ideas.what: Galois/monodromy action on the tower of Fermat curves as the metabelian quotient of π̂_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}), with values in Ẑ^*·(module over Ẑ[[Ẑ^2]])
ideas.modern_name: Ihara's Fermat-tower (metabelian) Galois representation / universal power series for Jacobi sums
ideas.usually_credited_to: Y. Ihara (1984–86, Annals 'Profinite braid groups, Galois representations and complex multiplications'); also Anderson, Coleman
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse explicitly as far as I know; Longue Marche manuscripts (unpublished)

ideas.what: Restricting the Fermat-tower representation along the section given by the rational point 1/2 recovers the Γ_Q → Aff(Ẑ) = Ẑ^*·Ẑ component (cyclotomic character plus a Kummer cocycle)
ideas.modern_name: Specialization of Galois action at a rational base point; Kummer characters arising from rational points/sections (cf. Nakamura, Ihara–Kaneko–Yukinari)

ideas.what: Programmatic statement: make essentially finite-type geometry over Q explicit through profinite group actions, and conversely describe geometric objects (the Fermat tower) group-theoretically
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983), Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

missed.claim: Around 1981 Grothendieck already used the Fermat tower (metabelian quotient) as the arithmetico-geometric interpretation of the Galois action on π̂_1(U_{0,3}). He also specialized it at the symmetric rational point 1/2 to isolate the Aff(Ẑ)-valued component. This anticipates Ihara's Fermat-tower/Jacobi-sum framework, which is credited to Ihara.
missed.quote: nous sommes arrivés à "décrire" la tour des courbes de Fermat, via l'hom (327) construit ici "à la force du poignet"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority and context for Ihara's theory. The explicit use of the section at z = 1/2 (fixed point of z ↦ 1−z) to extract a Kummer-type character may give a slightly different normalization from the literature, which mostly uses tangential base points.

missed.claim: The 'explicitation arithmético-géométrique' of Γ_Q → Ẑ^*·Ẑ is set up via a diagram but not fully computed here; in particular the exact Kummer character is not pinned down.
missed.quote: Il resterait maintenant à trouver une explicitation arithmético-géométrique de l'hom ... de Γ_Q dans Ẑ*.Ẑ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is minor. The answer is likely recoverable with standard Kummer theory, so it is probably not a real open problem.

deep.surprise_reason: The page shows Grothendieck working with the Fermat tower as the metabelian Galois representation of P^1 minus 3 points, years before Ihara's published theory, and specializing it at the rational point 1/2. This is a notable unpublished detail of historical interest. The mathematics itself was later developed independently and is now standard.
transcription_corrections: Throughout, 'G_{p,σ}' should read G_{ρ,σ}, consistent with the previous page.
'N_σ^{4ns}' / 'G^{4ns}' is the natural sign superscript ♮ (N_σ^♮, G_{ρ,σ}^♮), as transcribed on the next page.
'l'hom (323)' should be read as (326), and the arrow label '(322)' as (325), to match the surrounding pages.
'Mais [-cet hom-] utilisant le plongement' is correct: 'cet hom' is struck through.
'il m'importe' is uncertain in the image; it may read 'il s'agissait' or similar.
The superscript on the inserted 'ess.t' (essentiellement) modifies 'de type fini'.
'M^!' should read 𝓜^! (the calligraphic M of the previous page).
